title: Instant burst fallback starvation due to lease staggering and allocator lag
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Several customers experienced rapid 5xx errors and degraded throughput during short, intense traffic spikes (10-90s) on Dedicated reserved pools. Root cause is allocator lease staggering + lease-renew backpressure: when multiple allocator leaders staggered lease renewals and a subset entered a slow I/O path, the burst admission path failed to elect/renew capacity quickly enough. This produced immediate fallback to lower-tier pools and ultimately request shedding for a window of seconds, leading to customer escalations.

Why this is different: The failure mode is not a slow autoscaler or warmup delay — it's a timing-amplified allocator/lease choreography bug. Small clock/epoch jitter between allocator replicas combined with a pessimistic lease expiry grace led to a cascade where the burst admission circuit believed headroom was exhausted while physical GPU slots were available but not yet re-advertised.

Impact: Customer-facing 5xxs for premium tenants during microbursts, elevated latency for many more, and multiple support escalations from three enterprise customers between 2026-03-08 and 2026-03-09.

Goals: ship a targeted hotfix to restore deterministic lease re-advertisement and add longer-term guardrails (faster stale-lease reclamation, improved telemetry, and an autotuneable lease jitter window).
incident_timeline:
2026-03-08 09:12 UTC: Pager alerted on increased 5xxs for dedicated-reserved pool in us-east-1.
2026-03-08 09:17 UTC: Triage confirmed requests were failing admission checks even though GPU utilization averaged 45%.
2026-03-08 09:40 UTC: Temporary mitigation applied: reduced lease_grace_ms from 2500 -> 800 for the affected AZs (manual param push) to force faster reclamation; 5xx rate decreased but customer reported intermittent errors.
2026-03-09 02:30 UTC: Reproduced locally with a multi-replica allocator test harness by introducing a 150-400ms stall on one leader; observed burst admission denial within 3s of spike.
2026-03-10 14:05 UTC: Root cause confirmed - lease staggering + slow renew path. Created hotfix branch and tests.
2026-03-15 11:20 UTC: Canary of relaxed lease preemption + deterministic re-advertise patch running in us-east-1a with zero regressions so far.
reproduction_steps:
1) Deploy reserved-pool allocator with 3 replicas and enable burst admission.
2) Drive a 60s synthetic microburst (QPS ramp 0->800 in 5s) targeting a single tenant.
3) Inject I/O delay (200-500ms) into one allocator replica's lease renew path and jitter clock by +150ms.
4) Observe admission controller deny new slots for 2-6s despite free GPU memory and idle slots.

Notes: test harness located at ci-tests/allocator/lease-stress in internal monorepo.
mitigation_steps:
Short-term (live since 2026-03-08):
- Temporarily lowered lease_grace_ms for affected AZs to reduce stale-lease hang window.
- Enabled conservative fallback routing to warm cold-pools (slower but stable) for VIP tenants for 10 minutes when burst gating tripped.

Medium-term (this ticket scope):
- Hotfix: deterministic lease re-advertise on lease renew path and reduce stale-lease detection debounce.
- Add metric: lease_reannounce_latency and headroom_reconciliation_lag.

Long-term (follow-ups):
- Autoscaler calendar: add proactive pre-emptive re-advertise when burst predictor signals upcoming surge.
- Formalize lease jitter autotune based on observed leader liveness distributions across regions.
code_review_notes: PR 4567 added a deterministic callback on lease renew which forces re-advertise within the same epoch when renew latency > 100ms. Review feedback: Sam (Infra) requested additional unit tests around epoch rollover; Priya (SRE) asked for a kill-switch flag to revert behavior quickly. Implemented both. Need one more review from runtime owners.
tests_and_telemetry:
Added integration test 'lease-reannounce-flaky-leader' to CI that simulates renew path stalls.
Added two new Grafana panels: 'lease_reannounce_latency' and 'headroom_reconciliation_lag' under Dedicated > Autoscaler.
Alert: lease_reannounce_latency > 500ms for 30s triggers SES page.
postmortem_actions:
1) Ship hotfix to all regions (runtime-1.19-hotfix-lease-reannounce).
2) Add targeted alerting and an operator runbook to detect this exact symptomset.
3) Run a 72-hour targeted soak on reserved pools with synthetic microburst traffic.
4) Schedule follow-up to evaluate changing default lease_grace_ms and implement adaptive jitter (ENG-402722).
customer_comm:
Customer-facing summary prepared and approved by Support and SE: https://docs.redwood.ai/comms/2026-03-lease-incident-summary.
Outreach: Account managers notified three impacted customers on 2026-03-09 17:00 UTC with mitigation steps and ETA for full fix.
Follow-up: offered 10% credits for the affected billing period; legal cleared the message.
next_steps:
- Complete final review and merge PR 4567.
- Roll out hotfix to canaries in two AZs, monitor for 48 hours, then global rollout.
- Post-rollout: enable extended telemetry retention for lease metrics for 30 days.
- Open sibling ticket for adaptive lease jitter and autoscaler coupling improvements (ENG-402722).
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive lease preemption reduces transient 5xx but can increase allocator churn under noisy environments. We chose a deterministic re-advertise path with conservative default thresholds to minimize churn while restoring customer availability. Monitor for churn signal post-rollout.
approval_status: Engineering leads approved hotfix on 2026-03-12 (Marcus Chen).
owner_notes: Assigned primary to Jared Kim for patch and rollout coordination. SEs: coordinate with Kayla Rivera for customer comms and credit allocation.
resolution_criteria:
- Hotfix merged and deployed to all AZs.
- lease_reannounce_latency P50 < 120ms, P95 < 350ms across regions.
- No new customer 5xx incidents related to admission denials in the 7 days post-rollout.
- Postmortem written and distributed to Eng + Support.
